newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei falls through floor as bears reign.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei falls through floor as bears reign.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures took a beating in late Monday trade as concerns about further financial troubles at Japanese institutions and the slow speed of deregulation took their toll on an already depressed market.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract lost 705 points to close at 17,430 after dropping as low as 17,170. Volume was an active 26,025 lots.

A trader with a European futures house said sentiment was dented early by news that Kyotaru Co Ltd, a restaurant chain operator whose shares are listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's first section, had filed for protection from its creditors.
"It's the first time a first-tier company has gone under in over three years and the thinking was immediately, how many more are out there," said the trader.

The news spurred aggressive selling by U.S. hedge funds and the March Nikkei's failure to bounce back after the midday break fuelled another wave of selling, pushing the contract through the technical support level of 17,500.
Dealers said Nikkei cash and futures markets were also hurt by the Japanese government's failure to offer new economic initiatives in a closely watched policy speech in parliament.
"The market is unhappy with the type and speed of financial reforms," said the trader.
The dollar's strong hold above 117.50 yen and a bearish technical outlook were also cited as factors behind the slide.
But dealers said players might be wary of pushing the market lower before the end of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) branch managers' meeting on Tuesday.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract finished at 311.5 against its opening 309.6 on turnover of 254 lots.
